properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 8 at 2:54AM CDT until August 8 at 3:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO
properties.description:
The Flood Advisory will expire at 3 AM CDT early this morning for a
portion of southwest Missouri, including the following areas, Stone
and Taney.

Flood waters have receded. The heavy rain has ended. Flooding is no
longer expected to pose a threat. Please continue to heed remaining
road closures.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 8 at 3:48AM EDT by NWS Gray ME
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Coastal Waters from Cape Elizabeth, ME to Merrimack River, MA out
25 NM...
Waters from Cape Elizabeth ME to Merrimack River MA from 25 to 60
NM...

At 348 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a strong thunderstorm, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots. This thunderstorm was located
10 nm north of Jeffreys Ledge Buoy 44098, moving northeast at 25
knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until this storm passes.
properties.area: Coastal Waters from Cape Elizabeth, ME to Merrimack River, MA out 25 NM; Waters from Cape Elizabeth ME to Merrimack River MA from 25 to 60 NM

properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued August 8 at 1:43AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
At 141 AM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm
just west of Hueco Tanks, moving west at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
East, Northeast, and Far East El Paso, Chaparral, Mission Valley,
Clint, Horizon City, Hueco Tanks, San Elizario, Fort Bliss, Socorro,
Sparks, Homestead Meadows, and Agua Dulce.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.
properties.area: West Central Tularosa Basin/White Sands; Southeast Tularosa Basin; Western El Paso County; Eastern/Central El Paso County; Northern Hudspeth Highlands/Hueco Mountains; Rio Grande Valley of Eastern El Paso/Western Hudspeth Counties
properties.sender: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM

properties.title: Dust Advisory issued August 8 at 1:18AM MDT until August 8 at 2:45AM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Dust Advisory for...
Northwestern Hidalgo County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 245 AM MDT.

* At 116 AM MDT, sustained outflow winds from earlier thunderstorms
have been gusting between 40 and 50 mph around Lordsburg Playa.
Visibility along Interstate 10 has mostly been greater than 5
miles, but occassionally will drop to around 1 or 2 miles.

HAZARD...Visibility occassionally dropping to 1 or 2 miles with
strong winds up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Detected by National Weather Service meteorologists and
NMDOT weather stations.

IMPACT...Hazardous travel.

* This includes Interstate 10 in New Mexico between mile markers 1
and 19.

Locations impacted include...
Cotton City, Steins, Road Forks, Lordsburg Playa, Granite Gap, and
Pyramid Mountains.
properties.instruction:
Blowing dust brings reduced visibility, leading to dangerous driving
conditions. If driving, avoid blowing dust if possible. If caught in
dense blowing dust, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep
your foot off the brake.
properties.sender: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement issued August 8 at 3:14AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Coastal waters from Altamaha Sound to Fernandina Beach FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Fernandina Beach FL from 20 to 60
NM...

At 313 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated showers and a few
thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These
showers and thunderstorms were located along a line extending from
34 nm south of R2 Tower to 27 nm northeast of Amelia City, moving
north at 15 knots.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, and lightning strikes. Boaters should seek safe harbor
immediately until these storms pass.

Waterspouts are possible with this activity. If a waterspout occurs,
move your boat away from it. Waterspouts can develop rapidly and
produce winds and seas that are dangerous for vessels and everyone
onboard.
properties.area: Coastal waters from Altamaha Sound to Fernandina Beach FL out 20 NM; Waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Fernandina Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued August 7 at 11:37PM CDT until August 8 at 3:00AM CDT by NWS Springfield MO
properties.description:
At 1137 PM CDT, Department of Transportations reported flooding was
occurring from thunderstorms that produced heavy rain across the
warned area this evening. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mountain View, Willow Springs and Ozark National Scenic Riverways.

Highway 17 was reported to be closed due to flooding at Jam Up Creek.

This includes the following low water crossings...
Eleven Point River at County Road 1550, Gill Branch at Highway Y
and Elevin Point River at Highway U.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Many flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued August 8 at 12:14AM EDT until August 8 at 4:30AM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Rush County in central Indiana...
Shelby County in central Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 430 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1214 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Shelbyville, Rushville, Morristown, Fairland, Milroy,
Glenwood, Manilla, Arlington, Moscow, New Salem, Boggstown
and Marietta.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 8:14PM CDT until August 8 at 9:48PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 15.2 feet
just after midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late tonight.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued August 7 at 11:00AM AKDT until August 8 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1053 AM AKDT, the river remains in moderate flood stage
after heavy rains earlier this week, but is beginning to
subside. The river crested at 22.52 ft around 8pm Thursday,
August 7th.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 9:50am the stage was 22.3 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.



At 22.0 feet: McDougal's, King Point, Anglers Inn, Wilderness
Place, Lake Creek Lodge, 3-Rivers, and Cottonwood Resorts
will have water in a number of cabins with water also
encroaching the main lodge buildings.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
